skill.name: grasshopper-workflow
skill.description: Automates Rhino Grasshopper workflow creation through MCP, Python helpers, and CLI commands for components, connections, parameters, groups, and placement files.
skill.summary: Build and execute Rhino Grasshopper parametric modeling workflows from MMD and JSON planning files.
skill.author: AmemiyaLai

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Grasshopper component identifiers, Markdown code fences, import fallbacks, and high-entropy Chinese documentation with GUIDs. The confirmed risks are filesystem writes to user-supplied or workflow-controlled paths, which are expected for this automation skill but should be reviewed before execution.

remediation.issue: CLI and workflow commands can write JSON outputs to caller-provided paths.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict output paths to the project workspace or require explicit confirmation before overwriting existing files.

remediation.issue: The skill sends modeling commands to a local Grasshopper MCP server.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should run it only against trusted local MCP servers and review generated placement files before execution.

content.value_statement: Grasshopper models can require many repeated component, connection, and parameter steps. This skill provides a guided workflow and scripts for generating and executing those steps through MCP.
actual_capabilities: Creates Grasshopper components through a local MCP client using component GUIDs and canvas positions.
Connects components by source and target parameter names using saved component ID mappings.
Parses component_info.mmd files to extract components, connections, subgraphs, and slider values.
Generates placement_info.json command sequences from parsed MMD workflow descriptions.
Sets slider and vector component values and groups related components with optional colors.
Provides CLI commands for common parse, generate, execute, connect, and parameter tasks.
limitations: Requires a running Grasshopper MCP server on the configured host and port.
Assumes the referenced Grasshopper component GUIDs are valid for the local installation.
File writes use paths supplied by the user or workflow, so paths should be reviewed before execution.
The workflow guidance is specialized for Rhino Grasshopper parametric modeling tasks.

use_cases.title: Generate a parametric furniture model
use_cases.description: Turn a model specification into MMD component plans, placement commands, sliders, and Grasshopper component groups.

use_cases.title: Automate repetitive Grasshopper setup
use_cases.description: Create many components, connect them, and assign parameter values through scripted MCP operations.

use_cases.title: Document and replay design workflows
use_cases.description: Use component_info.mmd and placement_info.json to make modeling steps easier to review and repeat.

prompt_templates.title: Start a simple model plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a simple Grasshopper workflow for a rectangular table with adjustable width, length, height, and four legs.

prompt_templates.title: Create component documentation
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert a design into MMD structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this Grasshopper design into part_info.mmd and component_info.mmd steps: [describe the object, dimensions, and adjustable parameters].

prompt_templates.title: Generate placement commands
prompt_templates.prompt: Parse my component_info.mmd workflow and generate a placement_info.json sequence for adding components and connections.

prompt_templates.title: Review and execute a full workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Grasshopper workflow for missing connections, invalid GUID placeholders, slider ranges, and execution order before running it through MCP.

output_examples.input: Create a Grasshopper workflow for a table with adjustable top size and leg height.
output: A staged modeling plan with table top and leg subcomponents.
A component connection outline for sliders, planes, curves, extrusions, and final union.
A checklist for generating placement commands and setting slider values.

output_examples.input: Parse component_info.mmd and prepare it for execution.
output: A summary of detected components and connections.
A placement command sequence ready for review.
Warnings for missing GUIDs, positions, or connection parameters.

output_examples.input: Group the generated components by table top, leg base, leg placement, and final union.
output: Named component groups aligned with the modeling modules.
Optional group colors for visual organization.
A confirmation list of components assigned to each group.

best_practices: Confirm the Grasshopper MCP server is running before executing commands.
Review generated JSON paths and component GUIDs before allowing file writes or execution.
Use small test workflows before running large parallel component creation tasks.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated placement files before checking every component GUID and connection target.
Do not point output options at important project files unless overwriting is intended.
Do not assume the default localhost MCP endpoint is safe on shared machines.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates Grasshopper component creation, connections, parameter setting, grouping, and workflow execution through MCP and Python scripts.

faq.question: Does it require Rhino or Grasshopper?
faq.answer: Yes. It is useful only when a compatible Grasshopper MCP server is available.

faq.question: Can it generate placement_info.json?
faq.answer: Yes. It can parse component_info.mmd and generate a placement command sequence for execution.

faq.question: Can it query component GUIDs?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI and component manager include helpers for querying and mapping component GUIDs.

faq.question: Is it safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: Use caution. The scripts can write files and send commands to a local Grasshopper MCP server.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
